title: Bridge extensions to ACP v2 (draft)
description: Root type used only to generate `schema/bridge.schema.json`.

BridgeMeta.description: Added by the daemon under `_meta.bridge` on every `session/update` it sends.

seq.description: Position of this update in the session's log. Starts at 1 and has no gaps.

rootSessionId.description:
The session whose log this is, when the message belongs to a subagent's child session.
Absent when it equals the message's own `sessionId`.

UpdateOrigin.description: Under `_meta.bridge` inside an update body that the daemon wrote itself, not the agent.

agentId.description: The agent to create the session with. Absent for the daemon's first agent.

AgentInfo.description: One agent the daemon can start.

agentId.description: Stable id used in other calls, such as `claude` or `pi`.

version.description: Version of the adapter, when known.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation when the agent is not ready.

oneOf.description: Installed, but the user has to log in with the harness itself.

cwd.description: Only sessions in this working directory.

loggedOnly.description: Leave out sessions that only the harness knows. This never starts an adapter.

cursor.description: From a previous response, to get the next page.

live.description: True when an adapter process currently holds the session.

logged.description:
True when the session is in the daemon's log. False for a session only the harness
knows, for example one started in the harness's own UI: attaching to it, or sending it
anything, makes the daemon load its history from the harness first.

state.description: The last ACP `state_update` state, such as `idle` or `running`, when known.

headSeq.description: Sequence number of the newest update in the log.

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 time of the newest update.

AttachSessionRequest.description:
`_bridge/session/attach` request: start receiving a session's updates.

The response comes first, then the catch-up, then live messages.

afterSeq.description: The last sequence number the client has applied. Absent to get the whole session.

catchUp.description: How the client is brought up to date.

headSeq.description: Sequence number of the newest update at the time of the response.

oneOf.description: The updates after `afterSeq` follow. The client keeps its state.

A condensed replay of the whole session follows, ending with `replay_complete`.
The client discards its state for this session first.

DetachSessionRequest.description: `_bridge/session/detach` request: stop receiving updates. The session keeps running.

RequestResolvedNotification.description: `_bridge/request/resolved`: a pending approval or question was answered, possibly by another client.

requestId.description: The id of the request. It is the JSON-RPC id the daemon sent the request with.

method.description: The method of the request, such as `session/request_permission`.

params.description: The params of the request. Present in a replay, where the request itself is not sent.

outcome.description: The answer that was given, in the shape of the method's response.

resolvedBy.description: A label for the client that answered, when known.

SessionsUpdatedNotification.description: `_bridge/sessions/updated`: a session appeared or its summary changed. Sent to every app.

Scope.description: What a connected app may do. Each level includes the ones before it.

oneOf.description: Also create sessions, prompt, cancel, answer, change settings.
Also act as an extension: register a namespace, add items to sessions, serve methods.
Also manage the daemon. Nothing needs this yet.

RegisterExtensionRequest.description:
`_bridge/extension/register` request: this connection is the extension `namespace`.

From then on it may add updates whose kind starts with `x.<namespace>.` to sessions, and
the daemon passes it every request whose method starts with `_x/<namespace>/`.

AppendRequest.description:
`_bridge/session/append` request: add an update of the extension's own kind to a session.
It is numbered, stored, replayed and sent to every attached app like any other update.

update.description: The update body. Its `sessionUpdate` must start with `x.<namespace>.`.

state.description:
How the update changes what clients hold. Without it the update is kept as an event
that clients do not place among the items.

ItemRule.description:
How an extension's update changes client state: an ACP state rule whose target is the
update's own kind. The daemon stores it in the update under `_meta.bridge.state`, so every
client can apply it without knowing the extension.

id.description: Dotted path of the item's id in the update, such as `checkpointId`.

field.description: The field of the item that is changed. Absent means the whole item.

value.description: Dotted path of the new data in the update. Absent means the whole update.

seq.description: The sequence number the update got.
